query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix, whose overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation behavior across different temperatures remain unclear, what single intervention could improve its wear resistance under sliding conditions spanning different temperatures, friction velocities, and wear depths? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating tested under identical conditions, defines the operating limits of the prediction, cites supporting evidence from the introduction, and proposes a falsification experiment capable of resolving microscopic deformation during wear.

generation.hypothesis: Intervention: Milling for 10 hours; Material initial state: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix; Conditions: Sliding conditions spanning different temperatures, friction velocities, and wear depths; Structural mediator: Microstructure refinement and homogeneity; Mechanism: Hall-Petch strengthening effect and contamination; Predicted outcome: Improved wear resistance; Baseline: Unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating tested under identical conditions; Boundary: Limited by the extent of contamination; Uncertainty: Further research is needed to fully understand the effects of milling time on the microstructure and properties of the coating; Supporting evidence IDs: ["PMC11206460::chunk::000::abstract::6292b9f5e5", "PMC8510135::chunk::004::discussion::4c3fb0cd1b"]; Conflicting evidence IDs: []; Falsification experiment: Investigate the effect of milling time on the microstructure and properties of the FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix under sliding conditions

args.query: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix wear resistance and microscopic deformation behavior across different temperatures
